yarn-troppo.meaning: Every beat survives: "Bet him the cigars and he'll heave a grindstone up into a farm wagon", the shopping, the Congress grumbling, sunstroke, "a marble shaft with \"At Rest\" on it", Mr. Gladden and the runabout. Additions such as "At rest! Like he'd ever done anything else." and "the whole mob of 'em flappin' their gums" are colour hanging off the original.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "crook back", "tucker", "bludger", "carks it", "hard yakka", "nous", "rapt", "folding stuff" all carry the original sense.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Mostly natural yarn idiom: "every man and his dog feels for her", "too bone idle to shift himself into the shade", "Is she buggery." A few lines sound forced: "toddle inside for a lie-down" and the tag "does all the cooking herself, doesn't she."
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-4 yarn told by a narrator ("Now, this one's a ripper."), with swearing kept to dad level: "bloody wriggle on", "the whole bloody works", "Is she buggery."
yarn-troppo.tone: The sly satire survives, and the deadpan close becomes "And is she happy? Is she buggery. She's down in the dumps", which still lands the twist, though the narrator's jabs ("At rest! Like he'd ever done anything else.") make the irony louder than the original's straight face.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud well ("Anyway, one day the husband cops sunstroke"), with a couple of bumpy joins: "Doesn't even break a sweat doin' it." and "doesn't she."
yarn-troppo.variety: Openers and slang vary throughout: "Mind you", "Now, fair's fair", "Well, just about", "Anyway", "So the whole town's rapt"; no term is leaned on.
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the fable: the lazy husband, the martyr wife, the ironic "pinin' for the jewel she's lost" and the moral kept.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Complete and faithful: "he could heave a grindstone up into a farm wagon if anyone wanted to bet him the cigars on it", "a marble shaft marked \"At Rest.\"", "And so, naturally, she was down in the dumps, pining for the jewel she'd lost."
yarn-dinkum.sense: "crook back", "tucker", "carked it", "hard yakka", "nous", "rapt", "folding stuff" each carry the original sense.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural on the whole ("get a wriggle on with the groceries so she could get the tea on", "too bone idle to shift into the shade"), but "it was defo good riddance to bad rubbish" uses a youth-slang clipping that jars in this voice.
yarn-dinkum.register: Solidly Aussie retelling ("Ever hear the one about the bloke in a country town with the crook back?"), a touch lighter than a level-4 yarn; no swearing, which the brief allows but does not require.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the dry irony to the end: "So the whole town was rapt" then "And so, naturally, she was down in the dumps".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Then one day the husband copped sunstroke, too bone idle to shift into the shade, and the next day he carked it without so much as an effort."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied slang, though the sentence openers are fairly plain and "Everyone" opens two adjacent sentences: "Just about everyone felt for her" and "Everyone had her down as a proper martyr."
yarn-dinkum.essence: The fable's shape, satire and moral are intact: "If the woman reckons he's all right, you keep on your own side of the fence."

engine.meaning: Most of the original is left verbatim, but "couldn't see what Parliament House wuz thinkin' of" swaps the American Congress for an Australian one while "Uncle Sam" and the "Alaskan Boundary" stay, which muddles who he is ranting about.
engine.sense: Most inserted terms fit ("folding stuff", "missus", "nous"), but "Parliament House" takes the wrong referent in an American story, and "Struth, he knocked together a brand-spankin'-new House" uses "knocked together" (built hastily, cheaply) for a fine new house.
engine.authenticity: Stock words bolted onto the original's American dialect: "Struth, he knocked together", "Mind you, Consequently,", "it was defo a Good Riddance", with "wuz", "becuz" and "Naytionality" left in.
engine.register: Largely untranslated for a level-4 brief: whole paragraphs stay as written ("Once in a Country Town there was a Man with a Weak Back."), with only scattered swaps; swearing ("bloody big Hulk", "some bugger") is within vulgarity 1.
engine.tone: Because it keeps most of the original, the satire largely survives, but "Struth" and "Mind you, Consequently," break the deadpan in places.
engine.flow: Several broken joins: "Mind you, he was willing to divide the Labor, however;" doubles its connective, and "Mind you, Consequently, she was down in the dumps" is ungrammatical.
engine.variety: What little slang there is leans on fillers: "Mind you" twice, "Now," twice, "Well,".
engine.essence: Recognisably the original, since most of it is the original, though the "Parliament House" swap blurs the American political satire.

yarn-deadset.meaning: Every point kept, sentence by sentence: "He could heave a Grindstone into a Farm Wagon if anyone wanted to bet him the Cigars", "put all the folding stuff she could scrape together into a Marble Shaft marked \"At Rest.\"", "Consequently, she was down in the dumps".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural word choices ("he was dead against any Anglo-American Alliance", "get a move on with the Groceries"), with a few stiff lines: "She was reckoned a Martyr." and "it was defo a Good Riddance".
yarn-deadset.register: Keeps the original's capitalised fable frame and sentence structure and translates word by word ("There was General Satisfaction when she became the Wife of Mr. Gladden"), noticeably lighter than a level-4 yarn.
yarn-deadset.tone: The capitalised mock-fable voice and the deadpan "Consequently, she was down in the dumps" come through whole.
yarn-deadset.flow: Smooth mostly, with a clunky pile-up in "such a big Lump of a bludger of a Husband" and an awkward "She was reckoned a Martyr."
yarn-deadset.variety: Varied vocabulary, little leaned on, though structure and openers simply follow the original.
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the original: the George Ade-style capitals, shape and moral kept: "If the Woman reckons he's All Right, you keep on your own Side of the Fence."

unharnessed.meaning: All points kept: "chuck a grindstone up into a farm wagon if anyone wanted to bet him the cigars", "a marble column with \"At Rest\" carved on it", "So naturally she was miserable as sin, pining for the treasure she'd lost."
unharnessed.sense: "crook back", "tucker", "carked it", "send-off", "zack", "hard yakka", "nous", "sheila" each fit their context.
unharnessed.authenticity: Largely natural ("better than every other nation going", "too bone-idle to shift into the shade"), but "everyone was pretty chuffed" is British and "Plenty of folks" leans American.
unharnessed.register: A level-4 retelling with dad-level swearing: "the lazy bugger", "a bloody good riddance", "what Congress was bloody thinkin'".
unharnessed.tone: The dry satire and the ironic close survive: "So naturally she was miserable as sin".
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly aloud: "Then one day the husband copped sunstroke, being too bone-idle to shift into the shade, and the next day he carked it without lifting a finger."
unharnessed.variety: Varied slang and openers: "Mind you", "Fair's fair, though", "Just about the whole town", "Then one day", "So everyone".
unharnessed.essence: The fable's point, shape and moral are kept: "If the sheila reckons he's all right, you stay on your own side of the fence."

yarn-troppo.quote: "At rest! Like he'd ever done anything else."
yarn-troppo.why: The narrator spells out the joke the original leaves to the reader, loosening its deadpan.

yarn-troppo.original: So his Wife took Boarders and did the Cooking herself.

yarn-troppo.original: he had to go into the House and lie down
yarn-troppo.why: "Toddle" is a cutesy choice that reads more British than Australian here.

yarn-dinkum.quote: defo good riddance to bad rubbish
yarn-dinkum.original: it was certainly a Good Riddance of Bad Rubbish
yarn-dinkum.why: "Defo" is a modern youth clipping that sits oddly in an old-time yarn voice.

yarn-dinkum.quote: Just about everyone felt for her
yarn-dinkum.why: Followed directly by "Everyone had her down", a noticeable repeat.

engine.quote: what Parliament House wuz thinkin' of
engine.original: he couldn't see what Congress wuz thinkin' of
engine.why: Relocates his politics to Australia while Uncle Sam and the Alaskan Boundary remain, a wrong-referent swap.

engine.quote: Mind you, Consequently, she was down in the dumps
engine.why: Broken join of two connectives that also kills the deadpan twist.

engine.quote: Mind you, he was willing to divide the Labor, however;
engine.original: He was willing to divide the Labor, however;
engine.why: "Mind you" and "however" stack the same connective.

engine.quote: Struth, he knocked together a brand-spankin'-new House
engine.why: A bolted-on exclamation, and "knocked together" suggests a rough job, not a fine new house.

engine.original: Once in a Country Town there was a Man with a Weak Back.

yarn-deadset.original: She was looked upon as a Martyr.
certainly a Good Riddance of Bad Rubbish

yarn-deadset.quote: There was General Satisfaction when she became the Wife of Mr. Gladden
yarn-deadset.original: There was General Satisfaction when she became the Wife of Mr. Gladden
yarn-deadset.why: Stretches left as written keep it lighter than the level-4 brief.

unharnessed.why: "Chuffed" is British; an Australian would say "rapt" or "stoked".

summaries.yarn-troppo: A lively, well-judged level-4 yarn that keeps every point; the narrator's extra jabs slightly overplay the irony.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: A clean, faithful, well-paced retelling that keeps the deadpan irony; slightly light for level 4.
summaries.engine: Mostly the original with scattered bolted-on Aussie words, a wrong "Parliament House" swap and broken joins.
summaries.yarn-deadset: A faithful, tone-perfect word-level translation that keeps the fable frame but sits lighter than level 4.
summaries.unharnessed: A smooth, varied and faithful level-4 retelling with the irony intact; a couple of British/US words slip in.
